title: Manipulating and tracking single hepatocyte behavior during mouse liver regeneration by performing hydrodynamic tail vein injection
protocol: Prepare agarose gel by dissolving 1.2 g of agarose in 120 mL of TAE buffer using microwave at median power for 1-2 min.
Wait approximately 10 minutes for the gel to cool down before adding SYBR Safe DNA Stain (12 μL per 120 mL).
Pour the cooled gel gently into gel casters with combs, avoiding bubbles under the combs.
Gently swirl the stained gel and pour it into a gel caster with comb immediately after preparation.
PCR amplify gene of interest from parent plasmid using Infusion cloning primers.
Add 12.5 μL of Hifi PCR Premix to the reaction mixture.
Add 2.5 μL of Infusion primer 1 to the reaction mixture.
Add 2.5 μL of Infusion primer 2 to the reaction mixture.
Add 0.1–100 ng of DNA to the reaction mixture.
Add DNase/RNase-free water to 25 μL of total volume.
Run PCR using conditions in table 1 on the thermocycler.
Set up a few different reactions in parallel using different amounts of template DNA (e.g., 0.1 ng, 1 ng, 10 ng, 100 ng).
Carry out electrophoresis of PCR products on a 1% agarose gel to purify the amplicon.
Load 10 μL of a 1 kb ladder in the first lane.
Visualize DNA bands using a UV box.
Use a scalpel to cut the PCR band at 1383 bp containing E2F1 gene flanked by carrier-overlapping sequences.
Column purify the PCR fragment from the gel slice using the QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Add 5 volumes of Buffer PB to 1 volume of the gel containing the PCR band.
Apply mix to QIAquick spin column in collection tube.
Centrifuge and discard flow through.
Wash column by adding 0.75 mL of Buffer PE to the top of the column, repeat centrifugation, and discard flow through.
Centrifuge empty column in a new collection tube to remove excess buffer.
Place the column into a new 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Elute the DNA by pipetting 50 μL of buffer EB to the top of the column and centrifuge.
Double digest carrier plasmid (pT3-EF1-Nras-IRES-GFP) with restriction enzymes XhoI and EcoRI.
Grow bacteria from glycerol stock to amplify the plasmid so it can be isolated for further manipulation.
Pre-warm LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotic (in this case ampicillin) to 37°C.
Scratch surface of glycerol stock with a sterile pipette tip and return glycerol stock to −80°C.
Gently streak the LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotic to select for plasmid used.
Incubate the plate up-side-down at 37°C for 16 h.
Pick 4 colonies from plate and grow up each in 5 mL of LB media with appropriate antibiotic (in this case ampicillin).
Incubate for 8 h (day culture) in 37°C incubator shaking at 225 rpm.
Add 100 μL of the day culture to 30 mL of LB with appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate for 16 h in a 37°C incubator shaking at 225 rpm.
Harvest bacterial culture by centrifuging at 6000 × g for 15 min.
Resuspend bacterial pellet in 2 mL of Buffer P1.
Add 2 mL of Buffer P2, invert several times to mix, and incubate at 20°C–24°C for 3 min.
Add 2 mL of Buffer S3 to the mixture and invert several times to mix.
Load the mix into a QIAfilter Cartridge in a tube and incubate at 20°C–24°C for 10 min.
Gently insert the plunger into the QIAfilter Cartridge and filter the cell lysate into a tube.
Add 2 mL of Buffer BB to the filtered lysate and invert several times to mix.
Transfer lysate to a spin column on QIAvac 24 plus.
Apply vacuum until liquid has drawn through all columns.
Add 0.7 mL Buffer ETR to wash columns and apply vacuum until liquid has drawn through all columns.
Add 0.7 mL of Buffer PE and apply vacuum until liquid has drawn through all columns.
Centrifuge the columns at 10,000 × g for 1 min in a tabletop microcentrifuge to remove residual wash buffer.
Place columns into clean 1.5 mL tube, add 200 μL Buffer EB, and incubate for 3 min at 20°C–24°C to elute DNA.
Determine DNA concentration using the BioTek TAKE3 spectrophotometer.
Premix 400 ng of carrier plasmid in 10 μL.
Add 25 pmol of each sequencing primer (in 5 μL) for Sanger sequencing.
Mix the carrier plasmid and primers together.
Add 5 μg of plasmid DNA in 16 μL or less.
Add 1 μL (20 units) of XhoI.
Add 1 μL (20 units) of EcoRI.
Add 2 μL of CutSmart buffer.
Bring the reaction volume to 20 μL with DNase/RNase-free water.
Incubate at 37°C for 4 h.
Stop the reaction by heat inactivation at 65°C for 20 min.
Dephosphorylate DNA by adding 1 μL of alkaline phosphatase.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 h.
Carry out electrophoresis on the digested plasmid on a 1% agarose gel with 1 kb ladders.
Cut out the DNA band at 6683 bp representing the linearized carrier plasmid.
Column purify the linearized plasmid using QIAquick Gel Extraction Kit.
Insert PCR fragment or control insert into carrier plasmid via InFusion cloning.
Add 100 ng of gel purified PCR fragment.
Add 50 ng of gel-purified linearized vector.
Pipette 2 μL of 5× InFusion Premix Top into a total volume of 10 μL with DNase/RNase-free water.
Incubate the reaction for 15 min at 50°C in the thermocycler.
Stop the reaction by placing on ice.
Include both negative control (no PCR fragment) and positive control (2 μL of the control insert and 1 μL of the control vector from the InFusion kit).
Warm SOC medium to 37°C.
Thaw Stellar Competent cells in an ice bath just before use, mixing gently after thawing.
Transfer 50 μL of competent cells into a 14 mL round-bottom tube (falcon tube).
Do not vortex.
Add 2.5 μL of the In-Fusion cloning reaction from step 5 to the tube.
For negative control: add 2.5 μL of the In-Fusion cloning negative control reaction from step 5.
For positive control: add 2.5 μL of the In-Fusion cloning positive control reaction from step 5.
Place tubes on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock cells for exactly 45 seconds at 42°C in a water bath.
Place tubes on ice for 1–2 minutes.
Add pre-warmed SOC medium to bring the final volume to 500 μL.
Incubate by shaking (160–225 rpm) for 1 hour at 37°C.
Make a 1/100 dilution and a 1/5 dilution into 100 μL of pre-warmed SOC medium.
Centrifuge the remaining bacteria at 2000 × g for 5 minutes.
Resuspend the pellet in 100 μL of pre-warmed SOC media.
Plate bacteria in SOC media onto LB agar plates containing ampicillin.
Incubate plates upside down at 37°C in an incubator overnight (16 hours).
Pick 4 colonies from each experimental plate the next day.
Grow up each colony in 5 mL of LB media with appropriate antibiotic (ampicillin) for 16 hours in a 37°C incubator shaking at 225 rpm.
Retain 800 μL of transformed bacteria.
Mix retained bacteria with 200 μL glycerol by vortexing.
Store the mixture directly at -80°C.
Centrifuge LB media containing bacteria at 2000 × g for 10 min at 4°C to pellet bacteria.
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 250 μL of buffer P1.
Add 250 μL of buffer P2, mix by pipetting.
Add 350 μL of buffer N3, mix by pipetting.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 20°C–24°C.
Transfer 800 μL of supernatant to a QIAprep spin column and centrifuge; discard the flow through.
Wash the column with 0.5 mL of buffer PB; discard the flow through.
Wash the column with 0.75 mL of buffer PE; discard the flow through.
Elute DNA by adding 50 μL of buffer EB to the column, centrifuging and discarding the column.
Mix 400 ng of plasmid DNA (in 10 μL) with 25 pmol of each sequencing primer (in 5 μL).
Send the mixture to Genewiz for Sanger sequencing.
Add 1 μg of plasmid DNA to a new tube.
Add 1 μL of XhoI enzyme to the tube.
Add 1 μL of BstXI enzyme to the tube.
Add 1 μL of EcoRV enzyme to the tube.
Add 10 μL of NEB 3 buffer to the tube.
Add DNase/RNase-free water to a final volume of 100 μL in the tube.
Incubate at 37°C for 1 hour, then place on ice to stop the reaction.
Run the restriction digest reaction on a 1% agarose gel with a 1 kb DNA ladder.
Check for expected digestion pattern (For pT3-EF1A-HA-E2F1-IRES-GFP plasmid: expect bands at 5348, 1891, and 797 bp).
Verify the preparation contains only the expected plasmid by restriction digest.
Confirm no mutations were introduced during cloning through Sanger sequencing.
Repeat the cloning reaction from step 5 if undesirable products are observed in the restriction digest.
Prepare an LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotic at 37°C to select for the plasmid used.
Scratch the surface of the glycerol stock with a sterile pipette tip.
Return the glycerol stock to −80°C immediately after scratching.
Incubate the agar plate upside-down at 37°C for 16 hours.
Pick 4 colonies from the plate and grow each in 5 mL of LB media with appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate the cultures for 8 hours at 37°C shaking at 225 rpm.
Add 100 μL of the day culture to 30 mL of LB with appropriate antibiotic.
Incubate overnight for 16 hours at 37°C shaking at 225 rpm.
Isolate plasmid DNA using a Qiagen Midiprep EndoFree kit.
Determine the concentration of the isolated plasmid DNA using a BioTek TAKE3 spectrophotometer.
Thaw plasmids to be injected on ice.
For each 1 mL injection mix, combine 15 μg pT3-EF1A-HA-E2F1-IRES-GFP with 3.75 μg pCMV-SB13 and sterile saline.
Filter the injection mix through a 0.22 μm filter into a new 50 mL Falcon tube to ensure sterility.
Weigh the mouse.
Calculate the amount of plasmid solution to administer based on the mouse weight.
Prepare extra plasmid solution (approximately 10% more).
Draw up the calculated amount of plasmid solution into a 3 mL syringe with a 26 gauge needle.
Place the entire mouse body inside the restrainer, leaving its tail exposed.
Warm the bottom of the mouse tail under a heat lamp for 10 seconds.
Rapidly inject the mouse via the tail vein using the syringe held at a 10 degree angle to the vein within 5 to 7 seconds.
Take the mouse out of the restrainer and check for vitality signs (normal heartbeat and breathing).
Return the mouse to its original cage after injection.
Try different plasmid concentrations ranging from 5 μg to 30 μg/mL in mice under varying conditions.
Check injected mice after 1 week to count the number of GFP positive cells on tissue sections for initial optimization.
Use only the optimized concentration for subsequent injections.
Monitor mice at 2, 12, and 24 hours post-injection for signs of distress or drowsiness.
Euthanize mice immediately if they show persistent signs of distress.
Isolate GFP-expressing hepatocytes from the livers of hydrodynamically injected mice by in situ liver perfusion followed by FACS.
Extract RNA from isolated hepatocytes.
Quantify transgene amount and gene expression changes using real-time PCR.
Replace Perfusion medium I with Liver Perfusion Medium for collagenase-based liver perfusion technique.
Replace Perfusion medium II with Hepatocyte Wash Medium containing 0.05% w/v Collagenase for collagenase-based liver perfusion technique.
Resuspend the final hepatocyte pellet in PBS + 1% BSA + 0.1 μg/mL of DAPI on ice.
Perform FACS immediately after resuspension.
Mix 10 μL of cell suspension with 10 μL of Trypan Blue solution for viability assessment.
Load 10 μL of the mixture onto a hemocytometer.
Evaluate hepatocyte cell viability using a light microscope.
Count the total number of live cells from two random square grids out of nine using Trypan blue staining.
Determine the concentration of live hepatocytes as total number of cells from two square grids multiplied by 104/mL.
Electronically gate hepatocytes based on their forward and side scatter parameters using FACS isolation method.
Select single cells based on forward scatter-area and forward scatter-height.
Exclude DAPI positive cells as dead cells during sorting.
Sort the remaining cells into GFP positive and GFP negative fractions into 1 mL of TRIzol®.
Extract RNA from samples stored in TRIzol®.
Thaw sample in TRIzol®.
Add 0.2 mL of chloroform, vortex to mix.
Incubate for 3 min at RT.
Centrifuge samples at 12000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Carefully transfer the top aqueous phase to a new tube.
Add 0.5 mL of 2-propanol, incubate for 10 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge samples at 12000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Resuspend the RNA pellet in 75% ethanol.
Note: The pellet is very loose and may be dislodged easily; handle carefully when removing supernatant.
Centrifuge samples at 7500 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Airdry the RNA pellet for 10 min at RT.
Resuspend RNA pellet in DNase/RNase-free water, pipette up and down to mix.
Incubate RNA at 55°C–60°C for 15 min.
Determine RNA concentration using the BioTek TAKE3 spectrophotometer.
Add 1 μg RNA in 20 μL DNase/RNase-free water to cDNA EcoDry Premix.
Pipette up and down for up to 10 s to mix.
Incubate at 42°C for 60 min.
Stop reaction by incubating at 70°C for 10 min in PCR machine.
Pause Point: cDNA can be stored at −20°C or −80°C until real-time PCR.

Mix forward and reverse primers for each primer pair to make a primer stock containing 25 μM of each primer in DNase/RNase-free water (e.g., for 100 μL of primer stock: mix 25 μL of 100 μM forward primer solution, 25 μL of 100 μM reverse primer solution, with 50 μL DNase/RNase-free water).
Dilute cDNA to 5 ng/μL with DNase/RNase-free water.
For each reaction add 0.4 μL of 25 μM primer stock.
Add 4.6 μL of DNase/RNase-free water.
Add 5 μL of iQ SYBR Green Supermix.

Load samples into Axygen 384 Well PCR Microplate (pipette 5 μL of the appropriate cDNA or DNase/RNase-free water (negative control) into each well, then add 5 μL of the appropriate primer master mix).
Seal the plate with Axygen 384 Well PCR Microplate Seals.
Load plate into the Roche LightCycler® 480.
Calculate Ct values using the “Abs Quant/2nd Derivative Max” option in the LightCycler® 480 software.
Generate delta Ct values by normalizing average Ct values over triplicates to the endogenous control (e.g., Gapdh).
Normalize relative gene expression in the transfected hepatocytes to a reference sample (i.e., untransfected hepatocytes).
Hydrodynamically inject mice with transgene.
Perform partial hepatectomy (PH) on hydrodynamically injected mice at 7 days post-injection.
Sacrifice mice for liver immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence to determine the effect of transgene overexpression during liver regeneration.
Sacrifice mice at 30 h post-surgery for gene expression analysis.
Fix intact liver lobes in 10% formalin for 16 hours.
Transfer fixed liver lobes to 70% ethanol until paraffin embedding and sectioning, or follow an alternative fixation procedure involving sucrose/PBS steps ending with OCT compound embedding at -80°C.
Mount OCT embedded tissues onto a cryostat and section them to 10 μm thickness.
Place sections on positively charged slides.
Incubate sections in Acetone for 10 min at -20°C for antigen retrieval.
Rehydrate sections in PBS for 5 min.
Block sections in 3% BSA in PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Apply primary antibody (GFP and Ki67 antibodies diluted 1:400 in blocking solution) to the sections.
Incubate with primary antibody for 16 h at 4°C.
Wash sections three times with PBS, 5 min each at room temperature.
Apply secondary antibody (1:400 dilution of anti-Chicken Alexa Fluor™ 488 antibody and anti-Rabbit Alexa Fluor™ 647 antibody) in block.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash 3 times with PBS, each for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Add a drop of DAPI Fluoromount-G.
Slowly place a coverslip on top to avoid trapping bubbles and seal with nail polish.
Image mounted sections on a fluorescence microscope using the 10× objective (resulting in 100× total magnification).
Count the number of GFP and Ki67 double positive cells.
Normalize this count to the number of GFP positive cells to obtain the fraction of transfected hepatocytes initiating cell proliferation at 30 hours post-PH.
